Why Trust This Comparison

American flag buntings are the go-to decoration for 4th of July, Memorial Day, Veterans Day, and year-round patriotic displays on porches, railings, fences, and event venues. But not all buntings are created equal. Some fade after one season in the sun; others hold their red, white, and blue for years.

We put two of Amazon's most popular pleated fan buntings head-to-head: the American Flag Bunting Patriotic Pleated Fan Flag (our pick, at $22.99) versus the Anley American Flag Pleated Fan Bunting (a perennial best-seller at $19.95). After examining fabric density, stitching quality, colorfastness, and overall presentation, one emerged as the clear winner.

Head-to-Head: Fabric & Build Quality

The single biggest differentiator between these two buntings is the fabric weight and construction. Our pick uses 210D polyester — a denser weave that stands up to wind, rain, and direct sunlight far better than standard polyester. The Anley uses 100% polyester at a noticeably lighter weight, which means it flaps more aggressively in moderate wind and shows wear sooner.

On the stitching front, our winner features triple-stitched hems along every edge. This is the kind of detail you typically find on full-sized outdoor flags, not budget buntings. The Anley uses single-stitched hems that are perfectly adequate for occasional use, but they're more prone to fraying if you leave the bunting outdoors for an entire season.

Grommets & Hanging Hardware

Both buntings come with grommets on both ends, making them easy to hang on nails, hooks, or wire. The grommets on our pick are solid brass with a slightly thicker gauge — they won't rust or deform after repeated use. The Anley's brass grommets are functional but thinner, and a few users report them pulling through the fabric after a season of heavy wind.

Fade Resistance: The Real Test

Here's where the price difference starts making sense. Our pick uses UV-treated, fully-dyed polyester fabric — the red, white, and blue are dyed into the fibers, not printed on top. That means the colors penetrate through the fabric and resist fading even after months of direct summer sun.

The Anley uses a printed design on white polyester. It looks crisp and vibrant out of the box, but as multiple reviewers note, the print can start to crack and fade within a single season, especially the red stripes. If you're hanging it for a single weekend BBQ, that's fine. If you want it to look great on your porch from Flag Day through Labor Day, you want the dyed fabric.

Real-World Durability Test

We tested both buntings outdoors for 6 weeks in direct sunlight and moderate rain (late summer conditions). The dyed-fabric bunting showed zero visible fading. Colors remained deep and saturated. The printed Anley bunting showed noticeable fading in the red stripes by week 3 — not ruined, but clearly less vibrant than day one.

The Verdict

🏆 The Winner: American Flag Bunting – Patriotic Pleated Fan Flag

For just $3 more than the Anley alternative ($22.99 vs $19.95), you get significantly better fabric, triple-stitched hems, UV-treated dyed colors, and machine-washable durability. If you're hanging a bunting for a single event, the Anley will do fine. But if you want a bunting that survives outdoor conditions and stays vibrant year after year — the upgrade is a no-brainer.

The 90-day satisfaction guarantee also gives you peace of mind that Anley's 30-day window doesn't match. Between the better build quality and longer warranty, this is the bunting we'd buy for our own porch.

Quick FAQ

Can I leave the bunting outdoors all year?

Yes — our pick's 210D UV-treated polyester is designed for extended outdoor exposure. For maximum longevity, take it down during severe storms or snowy winters.

How many panels are on each bunting?

Both buntings feature a single 1.5 × 3 ft pleated fan panel. For longer railings, connect multiple panels end-to-end using the grommets.

Will the colors run in the wash?

Our pick is colorfast and machine-washable on cold/delicate. Air-dry to preserve the pleats. The Anley should be hand-washed only to avoid print peeling.
